questions.topic: ARIO Factor A (Atom Size and Electronegativity)
questions.question: Which of the following conjugate bases is the most stable according to the ARIO 'Atom' factor?

options.label: A
options.text: Fluoride anion (F⁻) due to highest electronegativity.

options.label: B
options.text: Iodide anion (I⁻) because the large, polarizable 5p orbital disperses negative charge over a larger volume than smaller halogens.

options.label: C
options.text: Methoxide anion (CH₃O⁻).

options.label: D
options.text: Chloride anion (Cl⁻).

questions.correct_answer: Iodide anion (I⁻) because the large, polarizable 5p orbital disperses negative charge over a larger volume than smaller halogens.
questions.explanation: Down a column in the periodic table, atomic size is the dominant stabilizing factor for conjugate base anions.

questions.question: Why is the pKa of phenol (~10) eight orders of magnitude more acidic than cyclohexanol (~18)?

options.label: A
options.text: The phenoxide conjugate base delocalizes negative charge across the aromatic ring (ortho/para positions) via resonance, whereas cyclohexoxide cannot.

options.label: B
options.text: Cyclohexanol contains an aromatic ring.

options.label: C
options.text: Phenol has a lower molecular weight than cyclohexanol.

options.label: D
options.text: Phenol is an ionic salt in water.

questions.correct_answer: The phenoxide conjugate base delocalizes negative charge across the aromatic ring (ortho/para positions) via resonance, whereas cyclohexoxide cannot.
questions.explanation: Resonance delocalization of the negative charge onto three aromatic ring carbons stabilizes the phenoxide conjugate base.

questions.question: Rank the following carboxylic acids in order of increasing acidity: acetic acid, chloroacetic acid, dichloroacetic acid, trichloroacetic acid.

options.label: A
options.text: Acetic acid (pKa 4.76) < Chloroacetic acid (pKa 2.86) < Dichloroacetic acid (pKa 1.29) < Trichloroacetic acid (pKa 0.65).

options.label: B
options.text: All four acids have identical pKa values.

options.label: C
options.text: Acetic acid is the strongest acid because it has fewer chlorines.

options.label: D
options.text: Trichloroacetic acid < Dichloroacetic acid < Chloroacetic acid < Acetic acid.

questions.correct_answer: Acetic acid (pKa 4.76) < Chloroacetic acid (pKa 2.86) < Dichloroacetic acid (pKa 1.29) < Trichloroacetic acid (pKa 0.65).
questions.explanation: Accumulating electronegative chlorine atoms increases inductive electron withdrawal through σ bonds, stabilizing the carboxylate anion.

questions.question: Why does the hybridization of carbon dictate the acidity order: ethane (sp³, pKa 50) < ethylene (sp², pKa 44) < acetylene (sp, pKa 25)?

options.label: A
options.text: Acetylene is an antiaromatic molecule.

options.label: B
options.text: sp³ orbitals are smaller than sp orbitals.

options.label: C
options.text: Ethane undergoes resonance delocalization.

options.label: D
options.text: Higher s-character in the hybrid orbital (50% in sp vs 25% in sp³) holds the carbanion lone pair electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus.

questions.correct_answer: Higher s-character in the hybrid orbital (50% in sp vs 25% in sp³) holds the carbanion lone pair electrons closer to the positively charged nucleus.
questions.explanation: Greater s-character places electron density closer to the positive nucleus, providing substantial electrostatic stabilization to the conjugate base.

questions.topic: Conjugate Base Stability and Acid Strength
questions.question: What fundamental relationship links conjugate base stability to the strength of a Brønsted acid?

options.label: A
options.text: Stable conjugate bases always correspond to weak parent acids.

options.label: B
options.text: There is no correlation between conjugate base stability and pKa.

options.label: C
options.text: The more stable the conjugate base anion (A⁻), the weaker the base and the stronger its parent conjugate acid (H-A, lower pKa).

options.label: D
options.text: Strong acids always have strong conjugate bases.

questions.correct_answer: The more stable the conjugate base anion (A⁻), the weaker the base and the stronger its parent conjugate acid (H-A, lower pKa).
questions.explanation: A more stable conjugate base corresponds to a smaller activation barrier for deprotonation and a lower, more favorable pKa.

questions.question: Why is tert-butanol (pKa 18.0) a weaker acid than methanol (pKa 15.5) in aqueous solution?

options.label: A
options.text: tert-Butanol has higher s-character than methanol.

options.label: B
options.text: tert-Butoxide is an aromatic anion.

options.label: C
options.text: The bulky tert-butyl group sterically hinders water molecules from closely solvating and stabilizing the negative charge on the tert-butoxide oxygen.

options.label: D
options.text: Methanol undergoes resonance delocalization.

questions.correct_answer: The bulky tert-butyl group sterically hinders water molecules from closely solvating and stabilizing the negative charge on the tert-butoxide oxygen.
questions.explanation: Steric encumbrance around the alkoxide oxygen impedes stabilizing hydrogen-bonding solvation by water molecules.

questions.question: What structural change occurs around the aluminum atom when AlCl₃ coordinates with diethyl ether?

options.label: A
options.text: Aluminum changes from trigonal planar geometry (sp², 120°) to tetrahedral geometry (sp³, ~109.5°) in the Cl₃Al←OEt₂ adduct.

options.label: B
options.text: Aluminum undergoes homolytic fragmentation.

options.label: C
options.text: Aluminum becomes octahedral (sp³d²).

options.label: D
options.text: Aluminum becomes linear (sp, 180°).

questions.correct_answer: Aluminum changes from trigonal planar geometry (sp², 120°) to tetrahedral geometry (sp³, ~109.5°) in the Cl₃Al←OEt₂ adduct.
questions.explanation: Accepting an electron pair into its empty p orbital rehybridizes aluminum from sp² trigonal planar to sp³ tetrahedral.

questions.question: Why is p-nitroaniline a much weaker base (pKa of conjugate acid = 1.0) than aniline (pKa of conjugate acid = 4.6)?

options.label: A
options.text: The nitro group donates electrons to nitrogen.

options.label: B
options.text: p-Nitroaniline is nonpolar.

options.label: C
options.text: The strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group delocalizes the nitrogen lone pair into its own oxygens via resonance, reducing electron availability for protonation.

options.label: D
options.text: The amino group in p-nitroaniline is positively charged.

questions.correct_answer: The strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group delocalizes the nitrogen lone pair into its own oxygens via resonance, reducing electron availability for protonation.
questions.explanation: Direct resonance conjugation between the amino lone pair and the para nitro group heavily depletes electron density on nitrogen.

questions.question: Why is guanidine [(H₂N)₂C=NH] one of the strongest neutral organic bases known (pKa of conjugate acid ~ 13.6)?

options.label: A
options.text: Guanidine forms covalent bonds with water.

options.label: B
options.text: Guanidine is an aromatic ring.

options.label: C
options.text: Guanidine contains a triple bond.

options.label: D
options.text: Protonation produces the guanidinium cation [C(NH₂)₃⁺], which is exceptionally stable due to symmetric resonance delocalization across three identical nitrogen atoms.

questions.correct_answer: Protonation produces the guanidinium cation [C(NH₂)₃⁺], which is exceptionally stable due to symmetric resonance delocalization across three identical nitrogen atoms.
questions.explanation: The protonated guanidinium cation is stabilized by three equivalent resonance contributors, sharing the positive charge equally across three nitrogens.

questions.topic: Solvent Dielectric Constant and Ion-Pair Dissociation
questions.question: How does solvent dielectric constant (ε) affect the dissociation equilibrium of an acid H-A into free ions?

options.label: A
options.text: Dielectric constant has zero effect on ionization.

options.label: B
options.text: High dielectric solvents prevent acid-base reactions.

options.label: C
options.text: High dielectric solvents (e.g., H₂O, ε = 80) effectively screen electrostatic attraction between H⁺ and A⁻, promoting complete ionization compared to nonpolar solvents (hexane, ε = 1.9).

options.label: D
options.text: Nonpolar solvents dissolve ions faster than water.

questions.correct_answer: High dielectric solvents (e.g., H₂O, ε = 80) effectively screen electrostatic attraction between H⁺ and A⁻, promoting complete ionization compared to nonpolar solvents (hexane, ε = 1.9).
questions.explanation: Coulomb's Law (F = q₁q₂ / εr²) shows that high dielectric permittivity reduces electrostatic attraction between ions, promoting dissociation.

questions.topic: Conjugate Base Stability and Acid Strength
questions.question: What fundamental relationship links conjugate base stability to the strength of a Brønsted acid?

options.label: A
options.text: Stable conjugate bases always correspond to weak parent acids.

options.label: B
options.text: There is no correlation between conjugate base stability and pKa.

options.label: C
options.text: The more stable the conjugate base anion (A⁻), the weaker the base and the stronger its parent conjugate acid (H-A, lower pKa).

options.label: D
options.text: Strong acids always have strong conjugate bases.

questions.correct_answer: The more stable the conjugate base anion (A⁻), the weaker the base and the stronger its parent conjugate acid (H-A, lower pKa).
questions.explanation: A more stable conjugate base corresponds to a smaller activation barrier for deprotonation and a lower, more favorable pKa.

options.text: tert-Butoxide is an aromatic anion.

questions.explanation: Steric encumbrance around the alkoxide oxygen impedes stabilizing hydrogen-bonding solvation by water molecules.
